Word frequencies used to time words (see word-frequency.js).

Derived from wordfreq 3.1.1 by Robyn Speer, https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq
(the most common 30,000 English and 20,000 French, Spanish, German, Italian,
Portuguese and Dutch words, with their Zipf frequencies rounded to a tenth).

Format: one line per Zipf value in tenths ("57" is 5.7), then the words with
that value, separated by spaces.

wordfreq's data is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike
4.0 license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/), and so are these
lists. wordfreq includes data from Google Books Ngrams, the Leeds Internet
Corpus, OpenSubtitles, SUBTLEX, Wikipedia, Reddit, Twitter and other sources;
see its README for the full list of sources and their terms.
